# The Engineering Behind What's Next — Cadence at CES 2027


17 Nov 2026


• 1 minute read


-
-
-
-


What does it take to build an intelligent machine that can understand its surroundings, make decisions, and interact with the physical world?


The answer goes well beyond AI. It takes advances in semiconductors, electronics, mechanical systems, software, power, thermal management, and simulation, all working together. And it takes new ways for engineers to design, explore, and validate increasingly complex systems before they enter the real world.


At CES 2027, Cadence will bring this engineering story to life under the theme **Design for AI. AI for Design. From Simulation to Reality.**


At the heart of the experience is a simple idea: **maximize possibility, build with certainty.** From semiconductor design and advanced packaging to electronics, multiphysics simulation, digital twins, and AI, Cadence technologies help engineers understand how individual components and complete systems work together.


[Physical AI](https://www.cadence.com/en_US/home/explore/what-is-physical-ai.html) brings this engineering challenge into sharper focus. Robots and intelligent machines are moving beyond predefined tasks toward systems that can perceive, reason, and act in dynamic environments. Designing them requires engineering that connects the digital and physical worlds, accounting for how hardware, software, and physical behavior interact.


From the chip to the complete system, there is much more to explore at CES, including how advances in engineering and AI are shaping the next generation of intelligent products and applications.


**Join Cadence at CES 2027, January 6–9, at LVCC West Hall, Booth #4218.**


This is where engineering possibility meets the physical world. More to come as we get closer to CES.
